maintainer_notes: WSIB loss-of-earnings rates index annually — confirm at wsib.ca/rates each January.
NPF Collective Agreement expires 2025 — check for renewal at npf-fpn.ca.
WSIA s.15.1 (PTSD) and s.15.3 (cancer) presumption schedules may expand — verify at ontario.ca/laws.
PHIPA s.52 response deadline is 30 days — confirm no amendments.
MFIPPA s.19 response deadline is 30 days; s.22 allows 30-day extension — confirm no amendments.
Update OPI routing if RCMP reorganizes national ATIP function.
NOT_offsets arrays are critical — verify on each annual update.
_meta.update_procedure: 1. Verify legislative citations at laws-lois.justice.gc.ca and ontario.ca/laws. 2. Confirm WSIB rates at wsib.ca. 3. Check NPF CBA status at npf-fpn.ca. 4. Bump version date. 5. Redeploy.

pipeda.full_name: Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act
applies_to: Private-sector organizations in provinces without substantially similar legislation

key_sections.s.4: Scope — applies to personal information collected, used, or disclosed in commercial activity
key_sections.Principle-9: Individual access to own personal information

pipeda.note: PIPEDA applies to private-sector health clinics, private insurance, and federally regulated employers. For public-sector employees (municipal police, fire, paramedics), MFIPPA/FIPPA is the primary access tool. For BC/AB private sector, PIPA applies instead of PIPEDA.

mfippa.full_name: Municipal Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act

key_sections.s.36: Personal access — individual's right to access own personal information
key_sections.s.14: Law enforcement exemption — applies to police records

mfippa.appeal_body: Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario (IPC) — ipc.on.ca
NOT_offsets: MFIPPA s.36 personal access requests cannot be denied solely for 'law enforcement purposes' — that exemption (s.14) applies to third-party records, not your own file

fippa.full_name: Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act
applies_to: Provincial institutions (OPP, provincial Crown agencies, ministries)

key_sections.s.14: Law enforcement exemption (same as MFIPPA but for provincial institutions)

fippa.appeal_body: Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario (IPC) — ipc.on.ca
fippa.note: OPP members use FIPPA (provincial). Municipal police (Toronto, Peel, Ottawa, etc.) use MFIPPA. If unsure, submit to the institution's FOI Coordinator and they will route it.

applies_to: Health information custodians: hospitals, physicians, EMS medical directors, pharmacists, long-term care homes

key_sections.s.4: Definition of 'personal health information' — includes ACRs, diagnoses, treatment records
key_sections.s.52: Right of access — individual may request own PHI from custodian
key_sections.s.3: 'Health information custodian' definition — EMS service is a custodian for ACRs

phipa.appeal_body: Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario (IPC) — ipc.on.ca
phipa.critical_distinction: ACRs (Ambulance Call Reports) are PHIPA records, NOT MFIPPA records. They document patient health information. A paramedic's own employment/HR records are MFIPPA records. These are two separate custodians and two separate access regimes.
NOT_offsets: PHIPA s.52 access cannot be denied without specific justification; IPC has broad oversight authority

applies_to: Schedule 1 employers: municipalities, fire departments, police services, EMS services

key_sections.s.15.1: PTSD presumption — PTSD in first responders is presumed occupational disease (proclaimed April 6, 2018). Applies to: police officers, firefighters, paramedics, dispatchers, correctional officers.
key_sections.s.15.3: Firefighter cancer presumption — listed cancers presumed occupational for professional firefighters with minimum service years (effective 2007, expanded 2014). Cancers include: bladder, brain, colorectal, esophageal, kidney, leukemia, lung, lymphoma, mesothelioma, multiple myeloma, prostate, testicular, ureter.
key_sections.s.15.3-minimums: Minimum service years by cancer type vary — e.g., bladder cancer: 10 years; mesothelioma: any duration; verify current schedule at wsib.ca

wsia.form_6_deadline: 6 months from date of injury or date worker knew/ought to have known condition was work-related
wsia.appeal_body: WSIB Appeals (internal); Workplace Safety and Insurance Appeals Tribunal (WSIAT)
NOT_offsets: WSIB benefits do NOT reduce PTSD presumption applicability — the presumption means WSIB cannot require proof of specific triggering event
WSIB loss-of-earnings benefits are generally NOT taxable

omers-act.full_name: Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System Act, 2006
applies_to: Municipal employees including municipal police, fire, and paramedics in Ontario
omers-act.pension_type: Defined benefit — 2% per year of service × average best 5 years salary
omers-act.disability_benefit: Early departure on medical grounds with enhanced pension calculations available
NOT_offsets: OMERS pension and WSIB can generally be received concurrently — verify with OMERS actuary for your specific situation

foippa.full_name: Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act
applies_to: BC public bodies: municipalities, police departments, Crown agencies

key_sections.s.5: Individual right to access own personal information

foippa.appeal_body: Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner for BC (OIPC BC) — oipc.bc.ca

applies_to: BC private-sector organizations — NOT public bodies
pipa-bc.note: Relevant to RCMP contract policing edge case: operational data generated under a BC Provincial Police Services Agreement may involve BC PIPA for private-party data. Federal RCMP employment records remain under the federal Privacy Act.

pipa-ab.note: Same RCMP edge case as BC PIPA — federal Privacy Act governs RCMP employment records; AB PIPA may apply to operational data from private organizations collected under RCMP contract policing.

ON.statute: WSIA, SO 1997, c 16, Sch A, s.15.1
covered_workers: Firefighters (professional, composite — confirm volunteer status with WSIB)
ON.how_it_works: PTSD diagnosed by a regulated health professional is PRESUMED to be an occupational disease. WSIB cannot require the worker to prove a specific triggering event. The employer can rebut only with strong contrary evidence.
ON.critical_tip: Reference WSIA s.15.1 explicitly on Form 6. Do not accept any denial that requires you to 'prove' the specific incident that caused the PTSD.
